purpose: Etonogestrel is used to prevent pregnancy. It is available as a small implant placed under the skin of your upper arm or as part of a vaginal ring. It is one of the most effective forms of birth control available.
how_it_works: Etonogestrel works mainly by stopping your body from releasing an egg each month, so there is no egg available to be fertilized. It also thickens the mucus in your cervix, making it harder for sperm to get through. Together, these actions make it very difficult for pregnancy to occur.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include changes in your menstrual period (irregular bleeding, lighter periods, or no period at all), headaches, acne, breast tenderness, mood changes, weight changes, and decreased sex drive. Some people may notice minor bruising or discomfort at the implant site.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, stroke, liver problems, unexplained vaginal bleeding, or certain types of cancer. This medication does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs). If you think you might be pregnant, contact your doctor right away. Some medications, including certain seizure drugs and antibiotics, may make it less effective.
typical_dosing: For the implant (Nexplanon): A small, matchstick-sized rod is inserted under the skin of your upper arm by a healthcare provider and works continuously for up to 3 years — no daily action needed. For the vaginal ring (NuvaRing): You insert one ring into your vagina yourself, leave it in for 3 weeks, remove it for 1 week, then insert a new one. Your doctor will guide you on the method that is right for you.
